channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG trapped below $60 as bears eye $55
item.description: Silver price advances by over 1.50% on Tuesday, even as US Treasury yields rise and the US Dollar remains firm. Concerns about a fragile truce deal between the US and Iran keep the XAG/USD trading at $58.73, above its opening price.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade persists, downside risk intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes that USD/CNH remains confined to a tight range, with the Dollar expected to trade between 6.7940 and 6.8080 in the near term.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar neutral as Fed rate hike bets stay alive
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) traded on a neutral stance near the 101.20 level on Tuesday as investors digested mixed United States (US) data and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary.

item.title: Gold rises above $4,000 yet poised for an 11% monthly loss
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price posts modest gains of 0.35% on Tuesday, set to end the month with losses of over 11% after retreating from monthly highs around $4,500 towards $4,000, weighed by overall US Dollar strength.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: US Dollar holds key support, bulls eye YTD high
item.description: The USD/CHF pair holds firm around 0.8070 on Tuesday, after losing 0.29% on Monday, supported by broad US Dollar (USD) weakness amid month-end flows and improving risk appetite.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Recovery faces resistance at 0.5700
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, supported by upbeat New Zealand business confidence data and a modest pullback in the Greenback. At the time of writing, NZD/USD trades around 0.5677, up 0.5% on the day.

item.title: BoE’s Bailey: “We have time to judge the pass-through of higher energy prices”
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Governor Andrew Bailey said in comments to CNBC that policymakers have time to assess how higher energy prices may feed through into the United Kingdom (UK) economy, while noting that financial conditions have already tightened.

item.title: Australian Dollar advances as hawkish RBA Minutes meet firmer US confidence data
item.description: AUD/USD trades higher near 0.6915 on Tuesday as investors digest the latest Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Meeting Minutes and a modest improvement in United States (US) Consumer Confidence.

item.title: Japanese Yen extends its fall as US-Japan rate gap underpins US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 162.65 at the time of writing, up 0.44% on the day, and remains close to its highest level in several decades.

item.title: Euro trims losses but Fed rate-hike bets keep gains in check
item.description: The Euro (EUR) stages a rebound against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as month-end repositioning weighs modestly on the Greenback, limiting support from upbeat US economic data. At the time of writing, EUR/USD trades around 1.1415 after hitting an intraday low of 1.1382.

item.title: British Pound holds firm as political stability offsets UK growth miss
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances 0.11% on Tuesday against the US Dollar (USD) despite UK data showing the economy is slowing, while the latest US jobs report indicated that the number of vacancies rose in May, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics.

item.title: Gold steadies after sliding to fresh seven-month low, Fed rate-hike bets weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds on Tuesday after falling to a fresh seven-month low of $3,941 in the Asian session, as dip buyers help the precious metal recover some of its losses. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,030 after hitting an intraday high of $4,063.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD attempts to reclaim $60 as bearish trend persists
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) edges higher on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) trims part of its intraday gains despite upbeat US economic data. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $59.70, up nearly 2.5% on the day.

item.title: Canada: GDP data signal firmer second quarter – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Abbey Xu notes that Canadian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 0.5% in April, beating Statistics Canada’s 0.4% advance estimate and marking the strongest monthly gain since July 2025.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack: “Inflation is still too high, Fed may need to consider rate hikes”
item.description: Beth Hammack, President of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Cleveland, told CNBC on Tuesday that the United States (US) economy remains resilient. The labor market is near full employment, and growth still looking solid.

item.title: United States: Labor stability tempers Fed hike risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ macro team led by Oscar Munoz expects headline US Nonfarm Payrolls to slow to 80k in June, with 55k private and 25k government jobs, marking a return to breakeven job growth. The Unemployment Rate is forecast to edge down to 4.2% as participation slips.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish bias sustained with one more hike – ING
item.description: ING’s Michiel Tukker and Benjamin Schroeder argue that reduced Oil sensitivity in rates and lingering uncertainty should prevent a strong dovish turn from the ECB.

item.title: Euro: Resistance at 1.1450 caps upside against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s FX strategists report that EUR/USD is softer as regional inflation data point to downside risks for national CPI, even as ECB President Lagarde signals that more tightening could come. Swaps price modest additional tightening by September.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Supported against Euro as NOK flows increase – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Senior Macro and FX Strategist Sara Midtgaard notes that the Norwegian Krone (NOK) weakened in June, with EUR/NOK peaking near 11.35, but now sees limited further upside.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains after Canada's GDP growth tops forecasts
item.description: USD/CAD trims its intraday gains on Tuesday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) strengthens after the latest Canadian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data surprised to the upside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4203 after hitting an intraday high of 1.4247.

item.title: WTI Oil advances amid improving Hormuz shipping, mixed risk outlook
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades higher on Tuesday, hovering around $70.80 per barrel at the time of writing, rebounding despite ongoing uncertainty surrounding relations between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Copper: China PMI support, US tariff risk – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht notes that the LMEX index remains under pressure even as China’s manufacturing PMI edges above 50, supporting Copper via AI-driven exports.

item.title: United States CB Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.2 in June
item.description: US consumer sentiment gains terrain in June, as the Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rises to 91.2 from May’s 90.6 (revised from 93.1).

item.title: Breaking: US JOLTS Job Openings increased to 7.594M in May
item.description: According to Tuesday’s Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), job openings totalled 7.594 million at the end of May.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Scope seen for recovery against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that recent improvements in Canadian growth data justify a more constructive view on the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that USD/JPY has broken above its 2024 highs near 162, reaching levels last seen in the 1980s, with traders focused on potential Bank of Japan (BoJ) action.

item.title: US Dollar: Modest upside scope as risks recalibrate – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong notes that the US Dollar (USD) softened slightly as global risk appetite improved on easing geopolitical tensions and a tech rebound.

item.title: Bank of England: No change expected in 2026 – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley outlines her baseline view on Bank of England (BoE) policy, citing softer United Kingdom (UK) Consumer Price Index (CPI), lower Oil prices and a slack labour market.

item.title: Economists Agree: 2026 Oil price forecasts lowered as Strait of Hormuz shipping improves – Reuters poll
item.description: According to a Reuters poll published on Tuesday, analysts have lowered their 2026 Oil price forecasts for the first time since the Iran war began as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz gradually improves, easing concerns over prolonged supply disruptions.

item.title: Euro stabilizes vs Yen amid softer German inflation, Japan intervention warnings
item.description: EUR/JPY trades modestly higher on Tuesday, hovering around 185.10 at the time of writing, up 0.07% on the day. The pair is supported by a resilient Euro (EUR) despite softer-than-expected German inflation data.
